title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', Grothendieck studies an automorphism of the profinite group π̂_{0,3} with multiplier μ ∈ Ẑ*. On the previous page μ = 1+2ν, where l_0^ν is the twist. The automorphism is described by a few objects:
- f = (r s; t u), with the sign ε of formulas (45)/(56): g ρ(g) ρ²(g) = ε and g = ε α ρ(α)^{-1}.
- α_0 = (a b; c d) with det δ = ad − bc.
- the matrices ξ = (A B; C D) and η = (R S; T U) in SL(2,Ẑ), images under π̂_{0,3} → Γ̂(2) ⊂ SL₂(Ẑ).
The previous page proved the theorem μD = 1 (58) and μU = ε (59). It also gave the explicit forms U = t² + u² and D = δ(c² + d² + cd).

This page identifies the signs arithmetically.

(1) ε = 1 iff μ ≡ 1 (mod 4), i.e. ν even; ε = −1 iff μ ≡ −1 (mod 4).
- Proof: 1/μ = εU = ε(t² + u²).
- Squares mod 4 are 0 or 1, so t² + u² mod 4 lies in {0, 1, 2}. Its only unit value is 1.
- U is a unit, so 1/μ ≡ ε (mod 4), i.e. μ ≡ ε (mod 4).

(2) The same argument for μD = 1 with D = δ(c² + cd + d²) gives δ = ±1 iff μ ≡ ±1 (mod 3).
- c² + cd + d² ≡ (c − d)² (mod 3) takes only the values 0 and 1 mod 3.

(3) Grothendieck packages this as (63): δ = ε_3(μ) and ε = D/U = ε_2(μ). Here ε_p is meant as a 'quadratic character' of μ at p. Knowing ε_3, ε_2, or both is equivalent to knowing μ mod 3, mod 4, or mod 12 respectively, using (Z/12)* ≅ (Z/3)* × (Z/4)* ≅ {±1}².

Modern reading: t² + u² and c² + cd + d² are the norm forms of Z[i] and Z[ω]. So ε and δ are the Dirichlet characters χ_{−4} and χ_{−3} evaluated on the cyclotomic character μ. Equivalently, they record the Galois action on i = ζ_4 and on √−3 (ζ_3). These are the orbifold points of order 2 and 3 of M_{1,1} (j = 1728 and j = 0). It is the familiar fact that the elliptic generators of SL₂(Ẑ) of order 4 and 6 are sent to conjugates of their μ-th powers, so the sign depends on μ mod 4 and mod 3.
errors: For p = 2 the statement 'ε_p = 1 iff μ ∈ (Z_p*)²' is inaccurate. Squares in Z_2* are 1 + 8Z_2, whereas ε = ε_2 depends only on μ mod 4. ε_2 should be the character μ ↦ μ mod 4, i.e. χ_{−4}, not the square-class character. For p = 3 the statement is correct.
The computations themselves (sums of two squares mod 4, x² + xy + y² mod 3) are correct.

ideas.what: Sign ε in g ρ(g) ρ²(g) = ε is determined by μ mod 4 via the norm form t² + u² of Z[i]
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on elliptic (order-4) inertia of M_{1,1}; quadratic character χ_{−4}∘χ_cyc
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in GT / profinite SL₂(Z) studies (Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, Ihara circle)

ideas.what: Determinant sign δ of α_0 equals μ mod 3, via the norm form c² + cd + d² of Z[ω]
ideas.modern_name: χ_{−3}∘χ_cyc; action on order-3/6 elliptic point (j = 0)

ideas.what: Joint data (δ, ε) equals μ mod 12

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, elementary identification of the signs in Grothendieck's explicit SL₂ model of GT-type automorphisms with the mod-4 and mod-3 quadratic characters of the multiplier. Nice link to the CM points j = 1728 and j = 0, but this is essentially standard knowledge about Galois action on elliptic elements of SL₂(Ẑ).
transcription_corrections: 'la formule pD = 1' should be 'la formule μD = 1'.
D = δ(c²+d²+cd) (plus sign, consistent with the previous page), not c²+d²−cd.
In (63), 'ε = D/μ' should read 'ε = D/U' (or U/D).
'caractère quadratique relatif à p, en μ dans (Z_p*)^{·2}' should read 'caractère quadratique relatif à p en μ', with ε_p = 1 iff μ ∈ (Z_p*)².

Margin reads approximately: 'en d'autres termes, on a μ ≡ ε (4). [En effet] dans U = t²+u² ≡ 1 (4), donc 1/μ ≡ ε (4), donc μ ≡ ε (4) — relation qui servait à la démonstration de μ ≡ δ (3) et idem ...'.
